notes: SHIP v1.14.408 - THE FORGE TOAST MOVES ABOVE THE ROW. Owner ruling, closing the one item v1.14.407 escalated rather than absorbed. THE 96px IS DELETED, NOT RETUNED - it was the last magic clearance in this stack and the twin of the 92px removed from .hint at .407, a constant describing a strip that used to declare no height. It failed the same way, and .407 made it total: the row grew to 58px, so the toast stopped merely clipping the row and began lying ENTIRELY inside it, hit-testable for its full four seconds over the pill strip. The clearance is now structural and identical to the caption's: #toast is a CHILD of .hud-bottom anchored at bottom:100%, so it clears the row and the focus card at ANY height with no number left to go stale. WHY THIS COULD NOT BE DONE AT .407, AND WHAT UNBLOCKED IT. Two requirements were in direct tension. The toast must clear the control row; it must ALSO paint above the OPEN detail panel, because the status-toggle handler fires with that panel up and a toast sealed underneath it takes the UNDO affordance with it - the technician silently loses the ability to revert a RACKED/PENDING change. Those could not both be true while .hud carried position:fixed, because a fixed element ALWAYS establishes a stacking context whatever its z-index, so any child was capped below the strip's own z-index:10 and therefore below the panel's 40. THE LEVER IS ONE DECLARATION: .hud moves to position:absolute with z-index:auto, which establishes NO stacking context, so the toast's own z-index:60 is resolved in #forge3d-hud's context and beats the panel (40), the search overlay (50) and the picker (55) - while .toprow and .herotag stay at auto and remain correctly covered by all three. The position change costs nothing today and is more correct tomorrow: #forge3d-hud is absolute inset:0 of the sheet and the sheet's rect was MEASURED identical to the viewport rect on both tiers, so the strip does not move a pixel - but it now anchors to the SHEET rather than the viewport, which is what it always described. That mismatch is inherited: the HUD came from a full-window mock where fixed was correct, and v1.14.233 fixed only the JavaScript half of it. TWO SMALLER THINGS FELL OUT. The left:50% + translateX(-50%) centring pair retires in favour of margin-inline:auto with width:fit-content, so the slide-in is now a plain translateY and the element carries NO transform at rest - a transform would make it a containing block for any future fixed descendant, which is the trap that cost v1.14.212. And --forge-gap is named in the token block, because 10px stopped being one element's cosmetic margin and became a SHARED term the moment the toast joined the caption in that slot: two elements restating the same number is how the next 92px gets born. THE CAPTION AND THE TOAST NOW SHARE ONE SLOT, so they are not allowed to stack: while the toast is up the caption yields via .toast.show ~ .hint, and it returns on dismiss over its own 800ms fade. This is why #toast is emitted BEFORE #hint in the markup - the sibling combinator needs that order. Both are getElementById lookups, so DOM position is irrelevant to the JS and showToast is unchanged. VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. Measured on WebKit at 390x844 and 834x1194, across a short focus card, the wrapping zero-state card and a forced three-line card: the gap above the row is exactly 10.0px in ALL SIX combinations, the toast never intersects the row or the card, and it stays inside the viewport. With the detail panel OPEN, document.elementFromPoint at the toast's own centre returns the toast and the UNDO span is hit-testable - the affordance survives. THREE FALSE FAILURES WERE FOUND AND FIXED IN THE PROBE, NOT IN THE CSS, and the method note is now in the spec so the next person does not repeat them: .toast animates translateY(20px) to 0 over 250ms, so measuring a rect in the same turn the class is added samples the element MID-FLIGHT and reports it up to 20px low; and .hint carries its own 800ms fade, not the toast's 250ms, so a 300ms wait catches it at 0.6 opacity on the way back. Also relearned: showToast is IIFE-scoped and unreachable at page scope, the same trap that bit the M2-b work, so the probe drives the exact DOM state it produces instead. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4559/4559 balanced (+1 deliberate: the caption-yields rule), CRLF intact with 0 lone LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep. RACK SCENE LOCK respected - nothing under #forge3d-mount, forge3d_render, drawGuts or the camera rig; this is the HUD layer outside the scene. ?legacy=1 unaffected - #forge3d-sheet is body.rd + .open gated and every selector here is scoped to it. GUARD: test/e2e/08-forge-layout.spec.js grows to 11 tests with three new ones that pin the OUTCOME rather than the CSS - the toast clears the row at every focus-card height, it still beats the open panel with UNDO hit-testable, and the caption yields and returns. Two of them assert the lever DIRECTLY (the strip must not be position:fixed and must not carry a z-index), so if anyone ever restores either, they fail here rather than in the aisle at 2AM. DEVICE-VERIFY, folded into the open batch pass: clear the service-worker cache, confirm v1.14.408, open the aisle and change a rack's loadout so the toast fires - it must appear ABOVE the pill row, never across it; open a rack's detail panel and toggle a row's RACKED/PENDING - the toast must be visible OVER the panel and UNDO must actually revert it; confirm the caption disappears while the toast is up and returns after; and confirm the bottom strip still clears the home indicator, which env(safe-area-inset-bottom) resolving to 0 in the harness means is verified by NOTHING off-device.
